screens.name: Home — default, omen fixture and transitions

findings: Increase the example-question whisper’s visibility consistently across atmospheric frames.

screens.name: Approach — opening and transition

screens.name: Ask — normal and transition

findings: Reduce unused question-field height for short questions while preserving expansion for longer input.

screens.name: Ask — enlarged input
screens.evidence: Sheet 1 shows the enlarged question and disclosure pushing submission below the viewport; supplied retained evidence reports successful scrolling and submission.
findings: Shorten the vertical lead-in to submission at 200% without shrinking enlarged text.

screens.name: Named-person editor — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 2–3 show selected Someone, labeled Alex input, privacy explanation and explicit save/cancel; runtime reports validation and identity retention.
findings: Give the selected-person row and name field slightly more visual separation.

screens.name: Named-person editor — 200%
screens.evidence: Sheet 1 shows readable enlarged identity controls and the save action near the viewport bottom.
findings: Reduce the gap between the wrapped heading and identity options so cancel remains easier to discover.

screens.name: Ask — named person collapsed, normal and transition

findings: Reduce the blank area between the question and identity row.

screens.name: Ask — collapsed named person and reader composer at 200%
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 20 show complete wrapped questions with submission extending below the first viewport; runtime reports enlarged composer navigation.
findings: Reduce vertical whitespace so enlarged users reach submission with less scrolling.

screens.name: Adaptive question 1 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 show a stable question, four spacious answer rows and numbered progress; runtime reports adaptive-question completion.
findings: Align answer wording with one dimension because progress from barely started to nearly certain mixes completion and confidence.

screens.name: Adaptive question 2 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 4 shows a consistent obstacle question and four separated answers with 2 of 3 progress.
findings: Show an unmistakable selected-answer acknowledgement before advancing.

screens.name: Adaptive question 3 — settled and transition

findings: Make the final answer’s transition into forecast preparation explicit.

screens.name: Other-answer editor — normal and transition

findings: Preserve the adjacent disabled-state explanation when validation changes.

screens.name: Other-answer editor — enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheet 5 shows readable enlarged input and Continue, with progress and Back to choices sharing a crowded top row.
findings: Allow progress and Back to choices to occupy separate rows at enlarged text sizes.

screens.name: Listening — voice failure and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 places microphone failure beside Type your question and Try voice again; runtime reports a repeated browser voice fallback.
findings: Retain typing as the prominent recovery route when microphone startup fails.

screens.name: Planning — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 18 shows planning-specific status, a time expectation, credit assurance and Cancel; runtime reports timeout and reduced-motion coverage.
findings: Preserve the explicit time and credit guidance throughout the wait.

screens.name: Research — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 22 changes the supporting status to context gathering while retaining the same loading structure and cancellation.
findings: Keep the stage-specific supporting status perceivable when research begins.

screens.name: Planning failure — settled and transition

screens.name: Forecast failure — settled and transition

screens.name: Sensitive question — planning redirect and transition

screens.name: Forecast reveal — settled and transition

screens.name: Check-in — unanswered and transition

screens.name: Check-in — Not quite saved

findings: Keep saved wording consistent between this view and History.

screens.name: Check-in — Not yet saved

screens.name: Evidence overview — settled, transition and reader 100%

screens.name: Evidence overview — reader 200%

screens.name: Assumptions — settled, transition and reader 100%

screens.name: Assumptions — reader 200%

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments based on the attached screenshots and supplied runtime account; no independent runtime checks were performed.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met for every screen or component; no definite hard-gate failure is established by the supplied material.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, excluding genuinely inapplicable dimensions.
Transition pairs support visual continuity of composition, but still images do not independently establish timing, focus behavior or absence of intermediate layout shifts.
Below-viewport content and partially visible controls are not treated as unreachable because supplied browser evidence reports scrolling and form completion.
Normal and enlarged coverage varies by screen; the layout summary does not replace an inspectable screenshot of every boundary or state.
Some form, eligibility and keyboard claims rely on explicitly retained earlier evidence rather than checks rerun this round.
Synthetic questions, repeated prose, truncated fixture strings and source labels do not establish production-copy defects or predictive quality.
The offline Sky and Circles screens demonstrate honest fallback behavior, not successful production social service operation.
Physical iPhone Safari, VoiceOver, native Dynamic Type, keyboard behavior, microphone operation, haptics and OS delivery remain unverified.
Simulated purchases do not establish real payment behavior; successful browser PNG downloads do not establish native share delivery.
DOM contrast results do not establish raster-image text contrast, and minimum browser bounds do not establish native hit testing.
No repeated novice-use study or representative physical assistive-technology study was supplied, so these scores do not certify full/native 9 or 10 quality.
topFixes: Reduce repeated headings, summaries and blank space at 200% so forms, evidence categories and primary actions are reached sooner.
Add semantic section headings to reasoning and meaningful question headings to answer readers.
Expose a direct scalable-text route beside share previews and improve the small preview’s qualification legibility.
Clarify selectable and navigable affordances for card answers, history rows and the forecast evidence link.
Clean up fixed-header scroll boundaries and rectangular smoke cutoffs while preserving the borderless mist direction.
Verify the remaining visual concerns with targeted normal/200% before-and-after captures, then complete the deferred physical accessibility pass.
